Black holes have a way out, says Stephen Hawking
So, where are these "way outs" in our universe?

First line of the article:

All is not lost if you fall into a black hole – you could simply pop up in another universe, according to Stephen Hawking.

AFAIK the idea is there might be alternate universes into which black holes spew data (stuff).

I think what pizza_mine was asking is this; if somebody in another universe fall into a black hole which leads to our universe, what does that look like? If our black holes are spewing shit into other universes, some other universes must have black holes spewing shit into ours, but where?

Ah I see. I am not even close to a physicist but IIRC the alternative universes are not like ours at all. I've heard it described as reverse universes where black holes operate as white holes and presumably they don't have black holes as we know them. Which is why we wouldn't have any white holes.

Not necessarily, the laws of physics between universes may differ in such a way that one universe might permit spewing it out even though ours doesn't -- with that being said, look up "white hole (relativity)".

My completely unfounded and uneducated hypothesis is that universes are nested within one another. The creation of a singularity in a parent universe results in the big bang of its child universe. The more deeply nested a universe is, the less massive and complex it would be.

I'm just a stoned guy who read a lot of shitty science books as a child though so who knows.

I think Stephen Hawking has jumped the shark. As a big fan it is hard for me to say this, but I knew this was coming. He has straight up violated Occam's Razor and a multitude of other scientific principals and grabbed headlines in the process.
